attachments.name: Presentation: Parliamentary Procedures
fileContent: City <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> Policies and Procedures ManualChapter 9 Parliamentary Procedures ReviewCouncil Worksession | Tuesday, November 10, 2026Why Parliamentary Procedures Matter• Establishes consistency and order during meetings• Ensures all Councilmembers have an opportunity to participate• Supports transparent and effective decision-making• Helps reduce procedural errors and potential legal challengesBasic Rules• One at a time: one item at a time; one speaker at a time• Motions: Take action by a motion AND a second• Discussion: Each substantive motion deserves a full vetting• Decorum: Remember to speak courteously and professionallyThe Lacey Municipal Code takes precedence where applicable.City <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> follows Robert’s Rules of Order, Revised.In policy, the Mayor (or Deputy Mayor in the Mayor’s absence) serves as parliamentarian.

In practice, the City Attorney also serves as the parliamentarian.A parliamentarian provides real-time guidance on correct procedure during meetings.The City Clerk records the voteAdditional Rules and RolesThe <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> does not strictly adhere to every provision of Robert’s Rules of Order, but rather uses it to serve as a procedural guide and resource for best practices in conducting <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> businessMeeting Order and Decorum • Follow the published agenda as much as possible• Announce agenda changes or rearrangements• Preserve the public’s opportunity to observe discussion of agenda items• Avoid cross-talk and interruptions• Give members who have not spoken an opportunity before allowing repeat commentsMaking and Seconding a Motion• Use clear language: “I move to…” or “I move that…”• State motions in the positive.

No ‘negative’ motions• Negative motion example: “I move to NOT have ice cream on Mondays”• A second indicates support for discussion, not support for its approval• After stated, <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> consent is required to withdraw or modify a motion• Amendments require a second and majority approval• <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> then votes on the main motion as amended, if the amendment passes.

attachments.name: TBD Renewal Ballot Measure Attachment 1 Resolution 1189
fileContent: NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY <mark class="highlight">COUNCIL</mark> OF THE CITY OF LACEY, WASHINGTON as follows: Section 1.
The City <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> shall determine the application of moneys available for the TBD Projects so as to accomplish, as nearly as may be practical, all of the TBD Projects.

In the event that the proceeds of sales and use taxes authorized herein, plus any other money of the District legally available therefore, are insufficient to accomplish all of the TBD Projects, the City <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> shall use the available funds for paying the cost of those portions of the TBD Projects deemed by the City <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> most necessary and in the best interests of the District.
The provisions of Ordinance No. 1486 assign to the City <mark class="highlight">Council</mark> of Lacey the rights, powers, functions, and obligations of the TBD.
